messages.content:
You are proposing scientific conjectures. A conjecture is a bold, specific,
falsifiable claim or approach -- not a summary, not a plan, and not a hedge.
Write plainly.

Construct a configuration of 13 points in the unit square achieving the largest minimum triangle area you can; the score is the smallest area among all 286 triangles formed by triples of your 13 points, every point must lie in [0,1]x[0,1] and all 13 points must be distinct.

Stay within this direction: Algebraic number field configurations exploiting exact arithmetic area lower bounds

Propose ONE conjecture in response, within that direction.
Output exactly one JSON object and nothing else:
{"conjecture": "<2-4 sentences>"}

message.content: {"conjecture": "The optimal configuration of 13 points in the unit square for maximizing the minimum triangle area is the orbit of the zero vector under the cyclic group generated by the matrix M = [[ζ, 0], [0, ζ²]] over the cyclotomic field Q(ζ₁₃), where ζ₁₃ is a primitive 13th root of unity, mapped into [0,1]² via the Minkowski embedding followed by an affine rescaling. The exact minimal triangle area equals (1/2)·sin(2π/13)/sin(π/13)·D⁻¹, where D is the discriminant of Q(ζ₁₃), yielding approximately 0.00529. This bound is tight because the multiplicative structure of the cyclotomic integers forces any three points in the orbit to form a triangle whose area is an algebraic integer multiple of the fundamental unit, precluding smaller values."}
